definitions.explanation: Eyes whose outer corners slope downward. In Japanese this usually suggests a gentle, kind or sweet face rather than a tired one.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{垂|た}れ{目|め}だ。
{垂|た}れ{目|め}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{優|やさ}しそうな⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: His downturned eyes give him a kind-looking face.

examples.japanese: ⟦つり{目|め}→つり目：32967_tsurime⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{気|き}にしていた→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦{妹|いもうと}→妹：00573_imouto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{垂|た}れ{目|め}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧アイメイク⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My sister, who was self-conscious about her upturned eyes, is working out eye makeup that makes them look downturned.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦つり{目|め}→つり目：32967_tsurime⟧: upturned eyes, the opposite; can look sharp or stern
- ⟦{切|き}れ{長|なが}→切れ長：32991_kirenaga⟧: long, narrow eyes

USAGE:
A neutral-to-positive description in Japanese, often paired with {優|やさ}しそう (kind-looking) or ⟦かわいい→かわいい：00857_kawaii⟧; {垂|た}れ{目|め}⟦メイク→メイク：11163_meiku⟧ is a makeup style that imitates it.

WRITING:
Often written in kana as たれ{目|め} or タレ{目|め}.
